newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Lyonnais shares extend gains.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais shares extend gains.

text.p: Powered by expectations of a strong profit recovery this year, shares in French state controlled bank Credit Lyonnais romped to a year high on Wednesday before retracing some gains.
The shares were up 2.88 percent at 282.50 francs at 0911 GMT after rising 6.5 percent on Tuesday. The blue chip CAC-40 index was up 1.74 percent.
Earlier the Credit Lyonnais shares rose 4.22 percent to 286.20 francs to set a new year high.
The climb came on the back of an article on Tuesday in the French business daily La Tribune which said the group's profit could hit two billion francs this year.
The bank, which nearly collapsed in the early 1990s under the weight of an ill-fated lending spree, has been restructuring its operations and cutting costs.
Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade predicted when the bank announced a 202 million franc net attributable profit in 1996 that 1997 profit would be "in the billions" of francs.

The newspaper quoted an industry source as saying that the two billion 1997 franc profit would be reduced to a net attributable figure of 1.5 billion because of a requirement under terms of the 1995 state rescue that stipulated it had to earmark a portion of its profits for the public purse.
